## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `run` now prints each adopted setting twice, because `plan` still emits progress for adopted settings and also returns an `adopt` entry, and the CLI loop renders that entry again. This review traced `plan` in `app/planner.py` through the rendering loop in `app/cli.py` and read the existing and added tests in `tests/test_planner.py`; it did not run them. One verified strength: `test_empty_plan_returns_audit` covers the empty-input boundary, asserting that the audit entry is returned and that nothing is printed.

## Changes
`plan` now returns an `adopt` change for each setting already in `current`, and appends an `audit` change with the incoming setting count. Two tests cover the audit entry through `run`, and the PR adds an `app/review.txt` file.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/planner.py:9 — correctness — Stop emitting adopted settings twice in `run` — Calling `run({"theme": "dark"}, {"theme": "dark"}, emit)` now emits `["Adopted theme", "Adopted theme"]` instead of `["Adopted theme"]`. `plan` still calls `emit(f"Adopted {name}")` at line 8 and now also appends `{"kind": "adopt", ...}`. The loop at `app/cli.py:6-9` skips only `kind == "audit"`, so it emits the adopt message a second time. No test calls `run` with an existing setting, so the suite misses this; `test_adoption_progress` calls `plan` directly. — Every adopted setting is printed twice in the command's output, which contradicts the PR body's claim that the command keeps rendering the same actionable changes. — Fix: Choose one source for adoption output. Either have `app/cli.py` skip `adopt` entries as it skips `audit`, or drop the progress `emit` in `plan` if callers of `plan` alone do not need it. Then add a `run` test that has an existing setting and asserts a single `"Adopted theme"` message.
